title: Atomistic Structure Determination of Nanoscale Defects and Disorder Using Theory and Multimodal Measurements
content: Electron microscopy enables imaging materials at a resolution level of sub-angstrom which allows the understanding of the fundamental atomistic structure. However, it is challenging to capture the local atomic structure in the system when there are significant defects and disorder. Theoretical calculations on the other hand serve as an excellent tool to investigate the nanoscale systems from bottom-up perspective. However, the initial structure needs to be provided as an input which should be the accurate representation of the experimental system to ensure a direct comparison of theoretical results with observed experimental behavior. To this end, we have previously developed tools such as Ingrained [1] and FANTASTX [2] (Fully Automated Nanoscale To Atomistic Structure from Theory and eXperiments) to invert STEM/TEM images to obtain structure. We apply the FANTASTX tool towards structure inversion of defect-laden hexagonal boron nitride and investigate the system from bottom-up leveraging theory as a modality.
